_about: The original's SCRIPT CLOCK: the whole milliseconds a frame gives the scripts, as a floor.
Planning step 147 of docs/planning/2026-09-11-magic-portals-remaster.md (program wave 3a, CK).
THE DECODE. The Android loop measures a frame as a float of milliseconds (gs2d Application.cpp
ComputeElapsedTimeF :36-50, off clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC): AndroidGLES2Video.cpp:66-69),
caps it at 1000 (android/main.cpp:180-181), and ETHEngine::Update hands it on twice
(ETHEngine.cpp:141-168): SetLastFrameElapsedTime(static_cast<unsigned long>(lastFrameDeltaTimeMS))
(:147) for the SCRIPTS, and the float itself to m_pScene->Update (:166) for the C++ side - the
physics step (ETHScene.cpp:464), the entities' own updates, and so their particle systems
(ETHSpriteEntity.cpp:453-459, :571-576). Confirmed in the shipped library: gs2d::ETHEngine::Update(float)
at 0xb4100 calls ETHDrawableManager::RemoveTheDead (+0x0e), then __aeabi_f2uiz at 0x1cb364 (+0x14) and
ETHScriptWrapper::SetLastFrameElapsedTime(unsigned long) at 0xf2038 (+0x18) (SE step 72). The script
reads that uint through sys:GetLastFrameElapsedTime directly, through the raw sys:UnitsPerSecond (the
credits' scroll: uint / 1000 x speed, ETHScriptWrapper.System.cpp:95-98) or through STimeManager
(out/parity/asbc/all_functions.txt, md5 48fe65ce8baea16b94ed84d8d7be84b0): getLastFrameElapsedTime,
bytes 7894..7961, ins 3-10 = fTOu(uTOf(GetLastFrameElapsedTime()) x m_factor); unitsPerSecond, bytes
8045..8162, ins 3-15 = speed x min(200, GetLastFrameElapsedTime()) / 1000. So the script sees 16 ms of a
16.667 ms frame, every frame: every scripted motion advances 4.17 % less than the wall clock says.
WHAT STAYS OFF THIS CLOCK: the physics step. The original's level world steps a FIXED 1/30 s whatever
the frame: Game::preLoop (ins 323) builds AverageFPSRateManager, whose constructor sets m_timeStep to
0.0333333f and whose manageFixedTimeStep calls sys:SetFixedTimeStep(true) and SetFixedTimeStepValue
(all_functions.txt bytes 231862..232274), and ETHPhysicsSimulator::Update steps m_fixedTimeStepValue
when the fixed step is on (ETHPhysicsSimulator.cpp:156-161); GetCurrentPhysicsTimeStepMS is then 33.33
(:165-168). So no floor reaches it. The port's own physics (SimulationClock.fixedDelta and
PhysicsSystem::Update) is untouched. On the engine's float, not this clock: the C++ side's particle
systems and the entities' lifetimes. WHAT STAYS ON THE WALL CLOCK: the scripts that read sys:GetTime or
sys:GetTimeF (EarthquakeGenerator::update, ETHCallback_portal's 400 ms kill, FadeInController - the menu
states' black and the level's two blacks, which the layer fades on m_menuClock.wallMs and
m_levelFrameWallMs - the world and level choosers' blink, the title animation, ScoreDashboard::loop): the
port's wall clock, the engine's tick. NOT on it, though a C++ drawer: ETHTextDrawer::Draw (the level's
'Part N' caption and 1-21's hint) is handed the floored uint, GetLastFrameElapsedTime(), by
ETHEngine::DrawTopLayer (ETHEngine.cpp:205), so it rides the script clock. The
reader-by-reader table is out/parity/program/CK/readers.md.
THE RATE. The floor depends on the frame rate the original is matched at, and the original's own target
is a 60 Hz display, so matched_hz is 60 and the floor is floor(1000 / 60) = 16 - derived in code
(ScriptClock::LoadRules: floor(1000 / matched_hz); there is no key of its own for it) and the value the sim
is handed for a tick, as exact whole milliseconds (n / 1000 and back is exact in a double for every n in
1..1000, so a threshold at a multiple of 16 trips on the tick the original's integer sum trips on).
Other rates, for the record: floor(1000 / 30) = 33 (loses 1 %), floor(1000 / 120) = 8 (4 %), floor(1000 /
59.94) = 16, floor(1000 / 144) = 6 (13 %); a frame the loop sees as 16.9 ms is 16 and one it sees as 17.0
is 17, so a real device jitters between the two where the port holds the nominal floor.
_physics_step_s: What the ORIGINAL's physics world advances in ONE frame, in seconds, whatever the frame's length: 1/30 s, so 2 x the 60 Hz
tick's 1/60. DECODED, Game::preLoop (bytes 112536..114414) ins 323 builds AverageFPSRateManager, whose constructor
manageFixedTimeStep (bytes 232198..232274) ins 3-10 calls sys:SetFixedTimeStep(true) and sys:SetFixedTimeStepValue(m_timeStep) -
from the constructor (ins 5-6) and again from every update (bytes 232143..232198 ins 3-4); ETHPhysicsSimulator::Update then steps
m_fixedTimeStepValue, not the frame (ETHPhysicsSimulator.cpp:156-161), and GetCurrentPhysicsTimeStepMS is 33.33
(:165-168). So at a 60 Hz frame the original's Box2D world runs TWICE as fast as the wall clock: a velocity a script sets covers
twice the distance per second the same velocity would at 30 Hz, and a body falls four times as fast in wall time (the
distance is a half g t^2 of a clock that runs twice as fast). The scripts that want a rate in wall time scale by
elapsed / 33.33 (applyForces, ETHCallback_minion, ETHCallback_dragon_knight); gravity and the portal recoil are not scaled, so they
run in the physics' own seconds. The footage bears it out: F10's zero-g recoil, scale(1.4) = 70 u per physics second, was
measured at 40-44 u/s on an emulator running 17-19 frames a second, 70 x 17/30 = 39.7 and 70 x 19/30 = 44.3 u/s
(out/parity/footage/F10.md section 3.1); at 60 frames a second the same shot is 140 u/s. The port's solver steps its own tick, so the
player - the one body whose velocity and gravity the port carries in the original's Box2D units - is carried at
SimRatio = physics_step_s / tick = 2 times the original's velocity (ScriptClock::SimRatio; planning step 148).
_matched_hz: the original's own target, a 60 Hz display, and the rate the port ticks at (MagicPortalsLayer::kTick); the CK step's spec builds the floor at that rate. The owner ruled nothing on the rate: it is the PORT-WIDE row's open question, answered here in favour of what the original does
_snap_ms: a frame within this of the tick's own length is the tick (the per-frame paths scale a frame's milliseconds by floor(1000 / matched_hz) / the tick's own length; the nominal frame must give exactly the floor) - the port's own arithmetic, not a decoded value
